nodes.title: 提示词
widgets_values:
How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 10.00-second mark of the target video.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action wuxia cinematography, one continuous shot. Begin exactly in the pose and framing of Picture 1: the adult East Asian woman holds a straight Chinese sword in her right hand, her right arm extended toward frame right and her left arm stretched behind her for balance. Preserve her facial identity, half-up long dark hair, red gemstone earrings, flowing orange patterned dress and scarf, sword and tassel, and the bamboo grove with warm backlighting.

From 0.00 to 3.50 seconds, she draws the extended sword inward, shifts her weight through a firm step, and pivots into one fast, fluid full-body turn. Her right hand guides the sword through a broad, controlled arc clear of her body, then brings the blade forward toward frame right. Her skirt flares, her scarf streams behind the turn, and her hair and sword tassel follow with delayed inertia. The camera makes a small lateral tracking movement at moderate speed, keeping her face, sword hand, and complete blade readable throughout the movement.

From 3.50 to 5.50 seconds, a single small pale-gold butterfly flutters into view from the upper right, above and clear of the blade's path. Her eyes notice it first. She deliberately checks the forward motion by softening her shoulder, slightly bending her elbow, and easing her wrist until the sword settles into a nearly horizontal position with its tip gently raised. Smoothly ramp from brisk action into pronounced slow motion during this deceleration. Her body becomes still before her skirt, scarf, hair, and tassel finish settling. The butterfly remains clear of the moving edge.

From 5.50 to 8.00 seconds, the butterfly makes a short, delicate approach above the now-steady sword tip, extends its legs, and settles on the flat upper surface of the blade just behind the point. Its wings tremble briefly, then open and close slowly. She keeps the blade steady, lowers her left arm gently, and follows the butterfly with her eyes. The camera pushes in slowly and shifts through a small arc toward a side three-quarter view, progressively bringing her face and the butterfly into the same composition.

From 8.00 to 10.00 seconds, her brows relax, her breathing settles, and the corners of her lips lift into a very slight smile as she watches the butterfly. A loose strand of hair drifts back beside her cheek while the butterfly gently opens its wings. Gradually settle into the exact pose, sword angle, butterfly position, framing, and lighting established by Picture 2 at 10.00 seconds. Preserve continuous physical movement through every speed change; no cuts, frozen frames, or abrupt pose changes. Keep one woman, one rigid straight sword held in her right hand, and one butterfly after its entrance. No dialogue, subtitles, or visible text.

overall_soundscape: Soft wind moves through bamboo leaves throughout the shot. The opening turn produces quick foot scuffs on earth, crisp sword swishes, and flowing fabric sounds, which lengthen and diminish as the movement slows. During the butterfly landing, only quiet bamboo rustling, faint fabric movement, and her soft settling breath remain.

non_diegetic_music: Rapid low drum beats and short plucked-string accents accompany the opening sword movement. As she notices the butterfly, the percussion drops away, leaving a sustained bamboo-flute note and sparse, soft string harmonics that fade toward the ending.
